name: Ibn al-Rumi
bio: Ibn al-Rumi was born in Baghdad in 221 AH (836 CE). His grandfather was of Greek origin and a client of the Abbasid family. He could spend a whole poem following one thought through its consequences, as in his elegies, or catch a physical movement in a few words. Al-Marzubani records how readily his praise of a patron could turn to satire. He died in Baghdad in 283 AH (896 CE), and the accounts of his poisoning differ.
